BS-P1-009 F02 §19 sets concurrent timers=10 and says any hard-ceiling excess must be rejected before Runtime; V09 only says aggregate Blueprint + per-Capability resource budget and does not define timer_count.
F02 ValidationReport requires resource_usage.timer_count, so timer_count is an externally observable validation result, not an implementation-private detail.

F04 ResourceBudget lists maxInstancesPerBlueprint, maxSerializedPropsBytes, maxLocalStateBytes, maxEventBindings, maxActionBindings and maxConcurrentTimers but does not define how any is measured or which validation/runtime stage owns enforcement.
Current generated validator registry gives maxConcurrentTimers=10 to every Phase-1 Core Capability because all definitions clone DEFAULT_RESOURCE_BUDGET; it therefore cannot identify timer consumers.
F04 logic.timer is TIME_DEPENDENT and has timer semantics, but no contract authorizes F02 to infer timer resource consumption from capability id, replayClass or prose.

F02 V04 explicitly requires availability=ENABLED, not REVOKED, dependencies available and Phase-1 execution class. GeneratedCapabilityValidator currently contains only validator, permission_class, resource_budget, compatibility and degradation.

Canonical CapabilityDefinition lifecycle has availability DISABLED|EXPERIMENTAL|ENABLED but no machine field for current REVOKED state; compatibility prose lists REVOKED as an outcome without a canonical source token.
generated/capabilities/compatibility-manifest.json carries availability and version ranges but no current revocation state; validator-registry.ts lacks availability/execution-class/revocation fields.

F02 service boundary names assertExecutable(contentHash,runtimeContext), but runtimeContext exact shape is absent. EXECUTION-ADMISSION defines a conceptual server flow but not trusted context shape, exact snapshot selection or deterministic denial precedence.

The public execution-admission endpoint concept takes content_hash, while implementation must not accept client-supplied trust/version/registry overrides; this boundary needs explicit machine truth for TEST-F02-012.

Current admitBlueprint preserves an existing REVOKED/INCOMPATIBLE trust_status on content reuse but still reports content status ADMITTED; contract must state that content persistence admission/reuse is never execution authorization.

F02 exact Blueprint schema has no trust_status/executable/module/handler/script fields and V10 forbids executable carriers. TEST-F02-009 must prove structural no-code safety, not reject inert user text merely because a string contains tokens such as eval or import.
